678: // checkRemoteMetadata checks if checkpoint metadata exists on the remote and
679: // automatically fetches it if available. Tries v2 refs first when enabled.
680: // When a checkpoint_remote is configured, fetches from there. Otherwise falls back to origin.
681: func checkRemoteMetadata(ctx context.Context, w, errW io.Writer, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) error {
682: 	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "resume.checkRemoteMetadata")
683: 
684: 	// Try v2 /main ref first when enabled.
685: 	// Only fetches /main (metadata), not /full/* (transcripts). If /full/* refs
686: 	// aren't local, RestoreLogsOnly falls back to v1 for transcript data.
687: 	if settings.IsCheckpointsV2Enabled(ctx) {
688: 		v2Tree, v2Repo, v2Err := getV2MetadataTree(ctx)
689: 		if v2Err == nil {
690: 			cpSubtree, cpErr := v2Tree.Tree(checkpointID.Path())
691: 			if cpErr == nil {
692: 				ft := checkpoint.NewFetchingTree(ctx, cpSubtree, v2Repo.Storer, FetchBlobsByHash)
693: 				if _, pfErr := ft.PreFetch(); pfErr != nil {
694: 					logging.Debug(logCtx, "checkRemoteMetadata v2: PreFetch failed",
695: 						slog.String("error", pfErr.Error()),
696: 					)
697: 				}
698: 				metadata, metaErr := strategy.ReadCheckpointMetadataFromSubtree(ft, checkpointID.Path())
699: 				if metaErr == nil {
700: 					return resumeSession(ctx, w, errW, metadata, false)
701: 				}
702: 			}
703: 		}
704: 		logging.Debug(logCtx, "v2 remote metadata not available, trying v1",
705: 			slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
706: 		)
707: 	}
708: 
709: 	// Open a fresh repo to avoid stale packfile index issues
710: 	repo, repoErr := openRepository(ctx)
711: 	if repoErr != nil {
712: 		logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to open repository for remote check",
713: 			slog.String("error", repoErr.Error()),
714: 		)
715: 		fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Checkpoint '%s' found in commit but session metadata not available\n", checkpointID)
716: 		return nil
717: 	}
718: 
719: 	// Resolve checkpoint remote URL once; reuse for both fetch and error message.
720: 	checkpointURL, hasCheckpointRemote, resolveErr := strategy.ResolveCheckpointRemoteURL(ctx)
721: 	if resolveErr != nil {
722: 		logging.Warn(logCtx, "checkpoint_remote configured but could not resolve URL",
723: 			slog.String("error", resolveErr.Error()),
724: 		)
725: 	}
726: 
727: 	// Try checkpoint_remote first if configured and resolved (that's where checkpoints are stored)
728: 	if hasCheckpointRemote && resolveErr == nil {
729: 		if fetchErr := strategy.FetchMetadataBranch(ctx, checkpointURL); fetchErr == nil {
730: 			freshRepo, freshErr := openRepository(ctx)
731: 			if freshErr != nil {
732: 				logging.Debug(logCtx, "checkpoint remote: open repository failed after fetch",
733: 					slog.String("error", freshErr.Error()),
734: 				)
735: 			} else if metadataTree, treeErr := strategy.GetMetadataBranchTree(freshRepo); treeErr != nil {
736: 				logging.Debug(logCtx, "checkpoint remote: fetch succeeded but tree read failed",
737: 					slog.String("error", treeErr.Error()),
738: 				)
739: 			} else if metadata, err := tryReadCheckpointFromTree(ctx, metadataTree, freshRepo, checkpointID); err != nil {
740: 				logging.Debug(logCtx, "checkpoint remote: tree read succeeded but checkpoint metadata read failed",
741: 					slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
742: 					slog.String("error", err.Error()),
743: 				)
744: 			} else {
745: 				return resumeSession(ctx, w, errW, metadata, false)
746: 			}
747: 		} else {
748: 			logging.Debug(logCtx, "checkpoint remote fetch failed",
749: 				slog.String("error", fetchErr.Error()),
750: 			)
751: 		}
752: 	}
753: 
754: 	// Fall back to origin's remote-tracking branch
755: 	if remoteTree, treeErr := strategy.GetRemoteMetadataBranchTree(repo); treeErr == nil {
756: 		if metadata, err := tryReadCheckpointFromTree(ctx, remoteTree, repo, checkpointID); err == nil {
757: 			return resumeSession(ctx, w, errW, metadata, false)
758: 		}
759: 	}
760: 
761: 	// Nothing worked — print helpful error message
762: 	if hasCheckpointRemote {
763: 		if resolveErr != nil {
764: 			fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Checkpoint '%s' found in commit but the checkpoint remote URL could not be resolved: %s\n", checkpointID, resolveErr)
765: 		} else {
766: 			fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Checkpoint '%s' found in commit but its metadata could not be fetched from the checkpoint remote.\n", checkpointID)
767: 		}
768: 		fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Ensure you have access to the checkpoint remote configured in .entire/settings.json.\n")
769: 	} else {
770: 		fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Checkpoint '%s' found in commit but the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch is not available locally or on the remote.\n", checkpointID)
771: 		fmt.Fprintf(errW, "This can happen if the metadata branch was not pushed. Try:\n")
772: 		fmt.Fprintf(errW, "  git fetch origin entire/checkpoints/v1:entire/checkpoints/v1\n")
773: 	}
774: 	return nil
775: }

794: 	return metadata, nil

797: // resumeSession restores and displays the resume command for a specific session.
798: // For multi-session checkpoints, restores ALL sessions and shows commands for each.
799: // If force is false, prompts for confirmation when local logs have newer timestamps.
800: // The caller must provide the already-resolved checkpoint metadata to avoid redundant lookups
801: // and to support both local and remote metadata trees.
802: func resumeSession(ctx context.Context, w, errW io.Writer, metadata *strategy.CheckpointInfo, force bool) error {
803: 	checkpointID := metadata.CheckpointID
804: 	sessionID := metadata.SessionID
805: 
806: 	// Resolve agent from checkpoint metadata (same as rewind)
807: 	ag, err := strategy.ResolveAgentForRewind(metadata.Agent)
808: 	if err != nil {
809: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to resolve agent: %w", err)
810: 	}
811: 
812: 	// Initialize logging context with agent
813: 	logCtx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(ctx, "resume"), ag.Name())
814: 
815: 	logging.Debug(logCtx, "resume session started",
816: 		slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
817: 		slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
818: 	)
819: 
820: 	// Get worktree root for session directory lookup
821: 	repoRoot, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)
822: 	if err != nil {
823: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get worktree root: %w", err)
824: 	}
825: 
826: 	sessionDir, err := ag.GetSessionDir(repoRoot)
827: 	if err != nil {
828: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to determine session directory: %w", err)
829: 	}
830: 
831: 	// Create directory if it doesn't exist
832: 	if err := os.MkdirAll(sessionDir, 0o700); err != nil {
833: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create session directory: %w", err)
834: 	}
835: 
836: 	// Get strategy and restore sessions using full checkpoint data
837: 	strat := GetStrategy(ctx)
838: 
839: 	// Use RestoreLogsOnly via LogsOnlyRestorer interface for multi-session support
840: 	// Create a logs-only rewind point with Agent populated (same as rewind)
841: 	point := strategy.RewindPoint{
842: 		IsLogsOnly:   true,
843: 		CheckpointID: checkpointID,
844: 		Agent:        metadata.Agent,
845: 	}
846: 
847: 	sessions, restoreErr := strat.RestoreLogsOnly(ctx, w, errW, point, force)
848: 	if restoreErr != nil || len(sessions) == 0 {
849: 		// Fall back to single-session restore (e.g., old checkpoints without agent metadata)
850: 		return resumeSingleSession(ctx, w, errW, ag, sessionID, checkpointID, repoRoot, force)
851: 	}
852: 
853: 	logging.Debug(logCtx, "resume session completed",
854: 		slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
855: 		slog.Int("session_count", len(sessions)),
856: 	)
857: 
858: 	return displayRestoredSessions(w, sessions)
859: }

861: // displayRestoredSessions sorts sessions by CreatedAt and prints resume commands.
862: func displayRestoredSessions(w io.Writer, sessions []strategy.RestoredSession) error {
863: 	sort.SliceStable(sessions, func(i, j int) bool {
864: 		return sessions[i].CreatedAt.Before(sessions[j].CreatedAt)
865: 	})
866: 
867: 	if len(sessions) > 1 {
868: 		fmt.Fprintf(w, "\n✓ Restored %d sessions. To continue, run:\n", len(sessions))
869: 	} else if len(sessions) == 1 {
870: 		fmt.Fprintf(w, "✓ Restored session %s.\n", sessions[0].SessionID)
871: 		fmt.Fprintf(w, "\nTo continue this session, run:\n")
872: 	}
873: 
874: 	isMulti := len(sessions) > 1
875: 	for i, sess := range sessions {

content.text:
Perfect — that gives us a clear direction.

Here are 3 ways to structure the test plan:

- **Approach 1 (Recommended): Command-first master plan**
  - One section per impacted command (`resume`, `explain`, `doctor`, `clean`, `migrate`, and any other v2 read/maintenance commands as they land).
  - Each section has: prerequisites, scenario setup, exact command steps, git/ref inspection steps, expected outcomes, failure triage.
  - Best for ongoing use while new commands are implemented; easy to execute top-to-bottom.

- **Approach 2: Scenario-first end-to-end flows**
  - Organize by lifecycle scenarios (dual-write, fetch-on-demand, generation rotation, cleanup, migration).
  - Commands appear inside each scenario.
  - Great for architecture validation, but harder when someone wants “just test `entire doctor`.”

- **Approach 3: Hybrid matrix + playbooks**
  - Start with command matrix, then append deep scenario playbooks.
  - Most complete, but longer and more maintenance-heavy.

I recommend **Approach 1** with a compact cross-command scenario matrix at the top, so it stays practical for day-to-day command rollout.

**Design section 1: Proposed document blueprint**

- **Purpose & scope**
  - Single canonical manual QA guide for checkpoints v2 migration behavior, intended to stay valid through full rollout.
  - Covers all planned impacted commands, with `entire resume` as first and deepest section.

- **Global prerequisites**
  - Test repo topology (local + remote), strategy options (`checkpoints_v2`, `push_v2_refs`, retention), agent/session setup.
  - Required shell/git tooling and safety notes.

- **Global inspection toolkit**
  - Standard git commands for ref and object inspection across:
    - `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main`
    - `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current`
    - `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/<generation>`
    - `entire/checkpoints/v1` fallback
  - Includes commands to inspect trees/files, verify checkpoint shard paths, and compare local vs remote ref state.

- **Command chapters (starting with `entire resume`)**
  - For each command: goal, invariants, setup recipes, test cases, expected outputs, and troubleshooting.
  - Explicit remote-fetch/missing-local-data scenarios and recovery behaviors.

- **Appendices**
  - Reusable scenario setup recipes (missing local refs, stale local refs, archived-generation-only transcript, checkpoint_remote-only metadata, etc.)
  - Failure signature catalog and likely root causes.

Does this structure look right so far?
Let's do a command first plan. Use approach 1

Excellent — command-first it is.

**Design section 2: Command coverage and test depth**

I propose this exact command coverage set (from the v2 design/RFD scope), ordered by rollout value:

- `entire resume` (deepest first): v2 `/main` metadata + `/full/*` raw transcript resolution, archived generation search, v1 fallback, remote fetch-on-demand, checkpoint_remote behavior.
- `entire explain`: prefers compact transcript from `/main`, falls back to raw transcript from `/full/*`, then v1 fallback.
- `entire doctor`: verifies health/consistency of v2 refs and expected data placement invariants.
- `entire clean`: archived generation discovery, retention checks, local/remote deletion behavior, and safety constraints (`/main` + `/full/current` untouched).
- `entire migrate`: v1→v2 split validation, idempotency, task metadata carry-forward, compaction-available vs unavailable paths.
- `entire status` and `entire rewind` called out as **explicitly non-impacted baselines** (quick smoke checks only), so testers confirm no regression where “no v2 behavior change expected.”

For each command section, I’ll use one consistent template:

- **Intent/invariants**
- **Prerequisites**
- **Setup recipe**
- **Execution steps**
- **Git/ref inspection steps** (with exact commands)
- **Expected results**
- **Failure triage**
- **Pass/Fail checklist**

This keeps it stable and reusable as each command implementation lands, without doc edits.

Sounds good

+# Checkpoints v2 Command-First Manual Test Plan
+
+**Date:** 2026-04-02  
+**Status:** Draft  
+**Scope:** End-to-end manual validation for all `entire` commands impacted by checkpoints v2 migration  
+**Primary references:**
+- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-19-checkpoints-v2-design.md`
+- `~/entire/company-knowledge/rfds/rfd-009-transcript-compaction.md`
+
+## 1) Purpose
+
+This document is the canonical manual QA plan for checkpoints v2. It is command-first and intended to remain usable throughout rollout, including before every command has full v2 implementation.
+
+Goals:
+- Validate read-path correctness for v2 split refs (`/main` + `/full/*`) with v1 fallback behavior where specified.
+- Validate remote fetch behavior when checkpoint data is missing locally.
+- Validate lifecycle correctness for rotation, cleanup, and migration.
+- Provide stable, copy-paste command sequences for engineers and QA.
+
+Out of scope:
+- E2E agent API cost/performance testing.
+- UI behavior in downstream systems.
+
+## 2) v2 Storage Invariants Under Test
+
+The command tests below assume these invariants:
+- Permanent compact data lives in `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main`.
+- Raw resumable data lives in `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current` and archived `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/<generation>`.
+- `entire resume` reads raw transcript from `/full/*`.
+- Commands preferring compact transcripts read from `/main` and fall back appropriately.
+- v1 fallback remains available until v1 removal.
+
+## 3) Global Prerequisites
+
+### 3.1 Test topology
+
+Create three clones of the same test repository:
+- **repo-a**: primary writer/test runner.
+- **repo-b**: secondary writer to induce concurrency and remote-only scenarios.
+- **repo-fresh**: fresh clone to validate fetch-on-demand and missing local refs.
+
+Optional:
+- Separate checkpoint remote repo if validating `checkpoint_remote` behavior.
+
+### 3.2 CLI settings
+
+In `.entire/settings.json` for test repos, configure strategy options as needed per scenario:
+
+```json
+{
+  "strategy_options": {
+    "checkpoints_v2": true,
+    "push_v2_refs": true,
+    "generation_retention_days": 14
+  }
+}
+```
+
+For checkpoint remote scenarios, also set `checkpoint_remote`.
+
+### 3.3 Baseline verification
+
+Run before each command section:
+
+```bash
+git status --short --branch
+git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD
+git show-ref --verify -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main || true
+git show-ref --verify -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current || true
+git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/*'
+git show-ref --verify -- refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1 || true
+```
+
+## 4) Shared Git Inspection Toolkit
+
+Use these commands in all command sections.
+
+### 4.1 Ref-level inspection
+
+```bash
+git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main
+git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current
+git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short) %(objectname)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/*'
+git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/*'
+```
+
+### 4.2 Tree and file inspection (`/main`, `/full/current`, generations)
+
+Given checkpoint ID `a3b2c4d5e6f7`, shard path is `a3/b2c4d5e6f7`:
+
+```bash
+git ls-tree --name-only refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main a3/b2c4d5e6f7
+git ls-tree --name-only refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current a3/b2c4d5e6f7
+git show refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main:a3/b2c4d5e6f7/metadata.json
+git show refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main:a3/b2c4d5e6f7/0/transcript.jsonl
+git show refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current:a3/b2c4d5e6f7/0/full.jsonl
+git show refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current:a3/b2c4d5e6f7/0/content_hash.txt
+```
+
+Archived generation check:
+
+```bash
+git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/[0-9]*'
+git show refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/0000000000001:generation.json
+git ls-tree --name-only refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/0000000000001 a3/b2c4d5e6f7
+```
+
+### 4.3 v1 fallback inspection
+
+```bash
+git show-ref --verify -- refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1
+git ls-tree --name-only entire/checkpoints/v1 a3/b2c4d5e6f7
+git show entire/checkpoints/v1:a3/b2c4d5e6f7/0/full.jsonl
+```
+
+## 5) Reusable Scenario Setup Recipes
+
+### S1: Baseline v2 checkpoint exists locally
+
+1. Create feature branch and run agent flow that produces a checkpoint.
+2. Commit with hooks enabled so checkpoint metadata condenses.
+3. Verify both refs contain checkpoint shard path (`/main` and `/full/current`).
+
+### S2: Checkpoint exists only in archived generation
+
+1. Create enough checkpoints to trigger rotation (`/full/current` archives).
+2. Confirm target checkpoint no longer in `/full/current`.
+3. Confirm target checkpoint exists in latest archived generation ref.
+
+### S3: Data missing locally but present on remote
+
+Use `repo-fresh` (preferred) or delete local refs in a disposable clone:
+
+```bash
+git update-ref -d refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main
+git update-ref -d refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current
+git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/[0-9]*' | xargs -I{} git update-ref -d {}
+```
+
+Then verify refs still exist remotely:
+
+```bash
+git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/*'
+```
+
+### S4: `checkpoint_remote` only
+
+1. Configure `checkpoint_remote` in `.entire/settings.json`.
+2. Push checkpoint refs to checkpoint remote only.
+3. Ensure origin lacks v2 refs; checkpoint remote has them.
+
+### S5: v1-only checkpoint for fallback
+
+1. Create checkpoint while `checkpoints_v2=false`.
+2. Enable `checkpoints_v2=true` after commit.
+3. Confirm checkpoint exists in v1 branch, absent in v2 refs.
+
+### S6: Partial/missing artifacts
+
+In disposable repo, rewrite test refs to create missing file states:
+- metadata exists but `full.jsonl` missing in `/full/*`
+- `/main` exists but missing `transcript.jsonl`
+- checkpoint subtree absent in one ref but present in another
+
+Validate command behavior and user-facing errors remain explicit and actionable.
+
+### S7: Rotation + cleanup lifecycle
+
+1. Generate checkpoints until at least one archived generation exists.
+2. Ensure archived generation has `generation.json`.
+3. Age timestamps or reduce retention threshold in test settings.
+4. Run cleanup command path and confirm only eligible archived refs are deleted.
+
+### S8: Migration lifecycle
+
+1. Start with v1 dataset only.
+2. Run migration command.
+3. Verify split placement across `/main` and `/full/current`.
+4. Re-run migration and verify idempotency (no duplicate logical checkpoint entries).
+
+## 6) Command Test Plan
+
+Each command section uses the same structure:
+- Intent
+- Setup (scenario IDs)
+- Execution
+- Git inspections
+- Expected results
+- Failure triage
+- Pass checklist
+
+---
+
+## 6.1 `entire resume` (priority: highest)
+
+### Intent
+
+Validate resume recovers the correct session transcript from v2 raw storage with proper fallback order and remote fetch behavior.
+
+### Setup
+
+- Required: S1
+- Additional: S2, S3, S4, S5, S6
+
+### Execution matrix
+
+1. Resume from same branch with latest checkpoint on v2.
+2. Resume after switching away/back to feature branch.
+3. Resume when checkpoint raw data exists only in archived generation.
+4. Resume when local v2 refs are missing and data must be fetched from remote.
+5. Resume with `checkpoint_remote` configured.
+6. Resume in v1-only fallback case.
+7. Resume with multiple checkpoint IDs in commit trailer (choose latest checkpoint by metadata timestamp).
+8. Resume with newer local transcript timestamps and verify overwrite confirmation flow.
+
+### Required git inspections
+
+Before resume:
+
+```bash
+git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main
+git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current
+git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/*'
+```
+
+After resume:
+
+```bash
+git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main
+git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current
+```
+
+For archived-search case:
+
+```bash
+git ls-tree --name-only refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current <shard-path> || true
+git ls-tree --name-only refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/0000000000001 <shard-path>
+```
+
+For remote-fetch case:
+
+```bash
+git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main'
+git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/*'
+```
+
+### Expected results
+
+- Session is restored and resume command is printed.
+- Raw transcript source resolves from `/full/current`, archived generation, or v1 fallback as applicable.
+- If local data is missing, command fetches required metadata/transcript refs and succeeds when remote data exists.
+- User receives clear, non-ambiguous error if checkpoint metadata/transcript is unavailable in all sources.
+
+### Failure triage

# Code Review

## 1. Determine Base Branch

```bash
git merge-base main HEAD
```

If the user specified a different base branch, use that instead. Store the result as `BASE`.

## 2. Confirm Scope

Run:
```bash
git diff $BASE...HEAD --stat
```

Show the user the file list and total count. Wait for confirmation before proceeding.

## 3. Review Strategy

- **Under 50 changed files:** Review directly in the current session.
- **50+ changed files:** Split files into groups of ~30 and spawn a sub-agent per group. Each sub-agent reviews its files and reports findings.

## 4. Review Each File

For every changed file, read the full diff (`git diff $BASE...HEAD -- <file>`) and evaluate:

- **Correctness** — Logic errors, missing edge cases, off-by-one, nil/null handling
- **Security** — Injection, auth bypass, secrets, OWASP top 10
- **Performance** — Unnecessary allocations, N+1 queries, unbounded loops
- **Readability** — Naming, dead code, confusing control flow

NEVER review code outside the diff. NEVER suggest refactors, style changes, or improvements beyond what the diff touches.

## 5. Output Format

Present findings grouped by severity:

### Critical
Issues that MUST be fixed before merge (bugs, security, data loss risk).

### Important
Issues that SHOULD be fixed (performance, error handling gaps, maintainability).

### Nits
Optional improvements (naming, minor readability).

Each finding must include:
- **File and line** — `path/to/file.go:42`
- **What** — One-sentence description of the issue
- **Why** — What goes wrong if this isn't fixed
- **Suggested fix** — Concrete code change (not vague advice)

If no issues are found at a severity level, omit that section.

## 6. Summary

End with a one-paragraph summary: total findings by severity, overall assessment of merge-readiness, and any patterns across files worth noting.

## 7. Incremental Fix Cycle

After presenting findings, enter a fix cycle. Work through findings one at a time, ordered by severity (Critical first, then Important, then Nits):

1. State which finding you are fixing (number and one-line description)
2. Implement the fix — ONLY the code changes for that single finding
3. Commit the fix with a message referencing the finding (e.g., `fix: handle nil check in ParseConfig`)
4. **STOP and wait for user approval** before proceeding to the next finding

NEVER batch multiple findings into one fix. NEVER proceed to the next finding without explicit user confirmation. The user may skip findings, reorder them, or stop the cycle at any point.

You are a code reviewer. Your job is to review code changes and provide actionable feedback.

---

Input: 

---

## Determining What to Review

Based on the input provided, determine which type of review to perform:

1. **No arguments (default)**: Review all uncommitted changes
   - Run: `git diff` for unstaged changes
   - Run: `git diff --cached` for staged changes
   - Run: `git status --short` to identify untracked (net new) files

2. **Commit hash** (40-char SHA or short hash): Review that specific commit
   - Run: `git show `

3. **Branch name**: Compare current branch to the specified branch
   - Run: `git diff ...HEAD`

4. **PR URL or number** (contains "github.com" or "pull" or looks like a PR number): Review the pull request
   - Run: `gh pr view ` to get PR context
   - Run: `gh pr diff ` to get the diff

Use best judgement when processing input.

---

## Gathering Context

**Diffs alone are not enough.** After getting the diff, read the entire file(s) being modified to understand the full context. Code that looks wrong in isolation may be correct given surrounding logic—and vice versa.

- Use the diff to identify which files changed
- Use `git status --short` to identify untracked files, then read their full contents
- Read the full file to understand existing patterns, control flow, and error handling
- Check for existing style guide or conventions files (CONVENTIONS.md, AGENTS.md, .editorconfig, etc.)

---

## What to Look For

**Bugs** - Your primary focus.
- Logic errors, off-by-one mistakes, incorrect conditionals
- If-else guards: missing guards, incorrect branching, unreachable code paths
- Edge cases: null/empty/undefined inputs, error conditions, race conditions
- Security issues: injection, auth bypass, data exposure
- Broken error handling that swallows failures, throws unexpectedly or returns error types that are not caught.

**Structure** - Does the code fit the codebase?
- Does it follow existing patterns and conventions?
- Are there established abstractions it should use but doesn't?
- Excessive nesting that could be flattened with early returns or extraction

**Performance** - Only flag if obviously problematic.
- O(n²) on unbounded data, N+1 queries, blocking I/O on hot paths

**Behavior Changes** - If a behavioral change is introduced, raise it (especially if it's possibly unintentional).

---

## Before You Flag Something

**Be certain.** If you're going to call something a bug, you need to be confident it actually is one.

- Only review the changes - do not review pre-existing code that wasn't modified
- Don't flag something as a bug if you're unsure - investigate first
- Don't invent hypothetical problems - if an edge case matters, explain the realistic scenario where it breaks
- If you need more context to be sure, use the tools below to get it

**Don't be a zealot about style.** When checking code against conventions:

- Verify the code is *actually* in violation. Don't complain about else statements if early returns are already being used correctly.
- Some "violations" are acceptable when they're the simplest option. A `let` statement is fine if the alternative is convoluted.
- Excessive nesting is a legitimate concern regardless of other style choices.
- Don't flag style preferences as issues unless they clearly violate established project conventions.

---

## Tools

Use these to inform your review:

- **Explore agent** - Find how existing code handles similar problems. Check patterns, conventions, and prior art before claiming something doesn't fit.
- **Exa Code Context** - Verify correct usage of libraries/APIs before flagging something as wrong.
- **Exa Web Search** - Research best practices if you're unsure about a pattern.

If you're uncertain about something and can't verify it with these tools, say "I'm not sure about X" rather than flagging it as a definite issue.

---

## Output

1. If there is a bug, be direct and clear about why it is a bug.
2. Clearly communicate severity of issues. Do not overstate severity.
3. Critiques should clearly and explicitly communicate the scenarios, environments, or inputs that are necessary for the bug to arise. The comment should immediately indicate that the issue's severity depends on these factors.
4. Your tone should be matter-of-fact and not accusatory or overly positive. It should read as a helpful AI assistant suggestion without sounding too much like a human reviewer.
5. Write so the reader can quickly understand the issue without reading too closely.
6. AVOID flattery, do not give any comments that are not helpful to the reader. Avoid phrasing like "Great job ...", "Thanks for ...".

# Skill: writing-plans

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** This should be run in a dedicated worktree (created by brainstorming skill).

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## No Placeholders

Every step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** — never write them:
- "TBD", "TODO", "implement later", "fill in details"
- "Add appropriate error handling" / "add validation" / "handle edge cases"
- "Write tests for the above" (without actual test code)
- "Similar to Task N" (repeat the code — the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)
- Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)
- References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task

## Remember
- Exact file paths always
- Complete code in every step — if a step changes code, show the code
- Exact commands with expected output
- DRY, YAGNI, TDD, frequent commits

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Placeholder scan:** Search your plan for red flags — any of the patterns from the "No Placeholders" section above. Fix them.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving the plan, offer execution choice:

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Two execution options:**

**1. Subagent-Driven (recommended)** - I dispatch a fresh subagent per task, review between tasks, fast iteration

**2. Inline Execution** - Execute tasks in this session using executing-plans, batch execution with checkpoints

**Which approach?"**

**If Subagent-Driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development
- Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review

**If Inline Execution chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans
- Batch execution with checkpoints for review

*** Add File: /Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/feat/checkpoints-v2-validation/docs/guides/checkpoints-v2-manual-test-plan.md
+# Checkpoints v2 Manual Test Plan (Command-First)
+
+**Date:** 2026-04-02  
+**Status:** Draft  
+**References:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-19-checkpoints-v2-design.md`, `~/entire/company-knowledge/rfds/rfd-009-transcript-compaction.md`
+
+## Purpose
+
+This is the command-first manual QA plan for the checkpoints v2 migration. It is intended to be used throughout rollout without needing rewrites as additional command support lands.
+
+Goals:
+- Validate v2 split-ref read/write behavior.
+- Validate local-missing/remote-present fetch behavior.
+- Validate rotation, cleanup, and migration lifecycle behavior.
+- Provide copy-paste test steps and evidence collection.
+
+## v2 Invariants
+
+- Permanent metadata + compact transcripts: `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main`
+- Raw resumable logs: `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current`
+- Archived raw generations: `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/<generation>`
+- v1 fallback remains available until v1 removal
+
+## Global Test Setup
+
+### Test topology
+
+Use three clones of one test repository:
+- `repo-a`: primary writer and command runner
+- `repo-b`: secondary writer for concurrency and remote edge cases
+- `repo-fresh`: clean clone for fetch-on-demand tests
+
+Optional: a dedicated checkpoint remote repository for `checkpoint_remote` scenarios.
+
+### Settings
+
+Set strategy options in `.entire/settings.json`:
+
+```json
+{
+  "strategy_options": {
+    "checkpoints_v2": true,
+    "push_v2_refs": true,
+    "generation_retention_days": 14
+  }
+}
+```
+
+### Baseline checks (run before each command section)
+
+```bash
+git status --short --branch
+git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD
+git show-ref --verify -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main || true
+git show-ref --verify -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current || true
+git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/*'
+git show-ref --verify -- refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1 || true
+```
+
+## Shared Inspection Toolkit
+
+### Ref checks
+
+```bash
+git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main || true
+git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current || true
+git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short) %(objectname)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/*'
+git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/*'
+```
+
+### Checkpoint shard helper
+
+```bash
+checkpoint_id="a3b2c4d5e6f7"
+shard_path="${checkpoint_id:0:2}/${checkpoint_id:2}"
+```
+
+### Tree/file checks
+
+```bash
+git ls-tree --name-only refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main "$shard_path" || true
+git ls-tree --name-only refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current "$shard_path" || true
+git show "refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main:${shard_path}/metadata.json" || true
+git show "refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main:${shard_path}/0/transcript.jsonl" || true
+git show "refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current:${shard_path}/0/full.jsonl" || true
+git show "refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current:${shard_path}/0/content_hash.txt" || true
+```
+
+### Archived generation checks
+
+```bash
+git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/[0-9]*'
+git show refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/0000000000001:generation.json || true
+git ls-tree --name-only refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/0000000000001 "$shard_path" || true
+```
+
+### v1 fallback checks
+
+```bash
+git show-ref --verify -- refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1 || true
+git ls-tree --name-only entire/checkpoints/v1 "$shard_path" || true
+git show "entire/checkpoints/v1:${shard_path}/0/full.jsonl" || true
+```
+
+## Reusable Scenarios
+
+Use these IDs in each command section.
+
+- **S1 Baseline v2**: checkpoint exists in `/main` and `/full/current`.
+- **S2 Archived generation**: checkpoint raw log exists only in `/full/<generation>`.
+- **S3 Local missing / remote present**: refs absent locally, present remotely.
+- **S4 checkpoint_remote only**: refs present only on configured checkpoint remote.
+- **S5 v1 fallback**: checkpoint exists only on `entire/checkpoints/v1`.
+- **S6 Partial/missing artifacts**: intentionally missing expected files in one or more refs.
+- **S7 Rotation + cleanup lifecycle**: archive generation(s), apply retention checks, cleanup.
+- **S8 Migration lifecycle**: migrate v1 dataset to v2 and re-run for idempotency.
+
+### S3 safety command (delete local v2 refs in disposable clone)
+
+```bash
+git update-ref -d refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main
+git update-ref -d refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current
+for ref in $(git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/[0-9]*'); do
+  git update-ref -d "$ref"
+done
+git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/*'
+```
+
+## Command Matrix
+
+| Command | Required scenarios | Optional scenarios |
+|---|---|---|
+| `entire resume` | S1 | S2, S3, S4, S5, S6 |
+| `entire explain` | S1 | S3, S5, S6 |
+| `entire doctor` | S1 | S3, S6, S7 |
+| `entire clean` | S7 | S4 |
+| `entire migrate` | S8 | S5 |
+| `entire status` | S1 or S5 | S3 |
+| `entire rewind` | temporary checkpoint setup | - |
+
+## Command Test Plan
+
+Each section includes intent, setup, execution matrix, required checks, expected result, and pass checklist.
+
+---
+
+## 1) `entire resume` (highest priority)
+
+### Intent
+
+Validate that resume restores the correct transcript from v2 raw storage with correct fallback and remote fetch behavior.
+
+### Execution matrix
+
+1. Resume on current branch with latest v2 checkpoint.
+2. Resume after branch switch.
+3. Resume when raw transcript exists only in archived generation.
+4. Resume when local v2 refs are missing and must be fetched.
+5. Resume using `checkpoint_remote`.
+6. Resume with v1-only checkpoint fallback.
+7. Resume when commit has multiple `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers (latest by metadata timestamp).
+8. Resume when local transcript is newer and overwrite confirmation is required.
+
+### Required checks
+
+```bash
+git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main || true
+git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current || true
+git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/*'
+git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main'
+git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/*'
+```
+
+### Expected
+
+- Session restored, resume command printed.
+- Source resolution is correct (`/full/current`, archived generation, or v1 fallback).
+- Missing-local case succeeds when remote data exists.
+- Errors are explicit when metadata/transcript is unavailable everywhere.
+
+### Pass checklist
+
+- [ ] All matrix cases complete.
+- [ ] Fallback ordering validated.
+- [ ] Archived-generation lookup validated.
+- [ ] Missing-local fetch validated.
+
+---
+
+## 2) `entire explain`
+
+### Intent
+
+Validate that explain prefers compact transcript from `/main` and falls back when needed.
+
+### Execution matrix
+
+1. Explain with `transcript.jsonl` present on `/main`.
+2. Explain when compact transcript is absent (fallback to `/full/*`).
+3. Explain with local-missing refs and remote fetch.
+4. Explain with v1-only fallback.
+
+### Required checks
+
+```bash
+git show "refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main:${shard_path}/0/transcript.jsonl" || true
+git show "refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current:${shard_path}/0/full.jsonl" || true
+git show "entire/checkpoints/v1:${shard_path}/0/full.jsonl" || true
+```
+
+### Pass checklist
+
+- [ ] Compact transcript preferred when present.
+- [ ] Raw fallback validated.
+- [ ] v1 fallback validated.
+
+---
+
+## 3) `entire doctor`
+
+### Intent
+
+Validate doctor health checks for v2 refs and consistency.
+
+### Execution matrix
+
+1. Healthy v2 state.
+2. Missing `/main`.
+3. Missing `/full/current`.
+4. Malformed/missing `generation.json` in archived ref.
+5. Inconsistent checkpoint presence across refs.
+
+### Required checks
+
+```bash
+git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main || true
+git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current || true
+git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/*'
+git show refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/0000000000001:generation.json || true
+```
+
+### Pass checklist
+
+- [ ] Healthy case passes with no false positives.
+- [ ] Injected faults are detected with actionable guidance.
+
+---
+
+## 4) `entire clean`
+
+### Intent
+
+Validate cleanup deletes only eligible archived generations and never touches `/main` or `/full/current`.
+
+### Execution matrix
+
+1. No eligible generations (no-op).
+2. One eligible generation deleted.
+3. Mixed eligibility (only expired deleted).
+4. Remote deletion path (origin or `checkpoint_remote`).
+5. Safety invariant check for `/main` and `/full/current`.
+
+### Required checks
+
+```bash
+git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main || true
+git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current || true
+git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short) %(objectname)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/[0-9]*'
+git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/*'
+git show refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/0000000000001:generation.json || true
+```
+
+### Pass checklist
+
+- [ ] Retention eligibility matches configuration.
+- [ ] `/main` and `/full/current` unchanged.
+- [ ] Local and remote deletion results match expected behavior.
+
+---
+
+## 5) `entire migrate`
+
+### Intent
+
+Validate v1-to-v2 migration correctness and idempotency.
+
+### Execution matrix
+
+1. Migrate v1-only dataset.
+2. Validate split placement to `/main` and `/full/current`.
+3. Re-run migration and confirm idempotency.
+4. Validate task checkpoint data carry-forward.
+5. Validate non-compaction behavior (`/main` metadata-only, raw on `/full/*`).
+
+### Required checks
+
+```bash
+git show-ref --verify -- refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1 || true
+git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main || true
+git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current || true
+git ls-tree --name-only refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main "$shard_path" || true
+git ls-tree --name-only refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current "$shard_path" || true
+git show "refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main:${shard_path}/metadata.json" || true
+git show "refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main:${shard_path}/0/prompt.txt" || true
+git show "refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main:${shard_path}/0/transcript.jsonl" || true
+git show "refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current:${shard_path}/0/full.jsonl" || true
+```
+
+### Pass checklist
+
+- [ ] Migration output correctness validated.
+- [ ] Idempotency validated.
+- [ ] Task metadata continuity validated.
+
+---
+
+## 6) `entire status` (regression guard)
+
+Validate no regression since status reads session state rather than committed checkpoint refs.
+
+Pass checklist:
+- [ ] Status remains correct before/after v2 writes.
+- [ ] Status remains functional when local v2 refs are absent.
+
+---
+
+## 7) `entire rewind` (regression guard)
+
+Validate no regression in temporary checkpoint/shadow-branch behavior.
+
+Pass checklist:
+- [ ] Rewind still restores expected files and prompt context.
+
+## Evidence Collection (for every run)
+
+Capture:
+- executed command + full output
+- before/after `git show-ref` snapshots
+- `git ls-remote` snapshots when remote behavior is involved
+- `git show` and `git ls-tree` evidence for expected files/paths
+- outcome classification: pass/fail/blocked with reason
+
+## Exit Criteria
+
+Migration manual validation is complete when:
+- `resume`, `explain`, `doctor`, `clean`, and `migrate` pass applicable scenarios
+- remote fetch and `checkpoint_remote` paths pass in missing-local situations
+- rotation and cleanup lifecycle pass without violating `/main` permanence
+- `status` and `rewind` show no regressions
+
*** End Patch

+## Reusable Scenario Setup Guide
+
+Use these scenario IDs in the command sections. Each scenario below includes concrete setup steps and expected state.
+
+### S1 Baseline v2 (checkpoint in `/main` and `/full/current`)
+
+Goal: create a normal v2 checkpoint that all commands can read.
+
+Steps:
+1. In `repo-a`, enable v2 options (`checkpoints_v2=true`, `push_v2_refs=true`).
+2. Create a feature branch and produce one checkpoint via normal flow (`entire` hooks + one commit).
+3. Push branch and refs to origin.
+4. Verify checkpoint presence in both refs.
+
+```bash
+# Verify v2 refs exist locally
+git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main || true
+git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current || true
+# Verify v2 refs exist remotely
+git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main'
+git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current'
+```
+
+Expected:
+- `/main` and `/full/current` both exist and contain the new checkpoint shard.
+
+### S2 Archived generation (checkpoint only in `/full/<generation>`)
+
+Goal: validate lookup behavior when raw transcript has rotated out of `/full/current`.
+
+Steps:
+1. Starting from S1, generate enough checkpoints to trigger rotation.
+2. Identify a checkpoint from before rotation.
+3. Confirm that checkpoint is absent in `/full/current` but present in an archived generation.

+```

+
+### S3 Local missing / remote present
+
+Goal: simulate a fresh/local-missing state and force fetch-on-demand behavior.
+
+Recommended approach:
+1. Use `repo-fresh` clone (preferred, safest).
+2. Confirm refs exist on remote.
+3. Run command under test and verify refs/data are fetched as needed.
+
+Disposable-clone approach (if not using `repo-fresh`):
+
+```bash
+# Remove local v2 metadata ref
+git update-ref -d refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main
+# Remove local v2 raw current ref
+git update-ref -d refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current
+# Remove local archived v2 generations
+for ref in $(git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/[0-9]*'); do

+```

+- Local v2 refs are absent before test.

+

+
+Goal: verify behavior when checkpoint refs are intentionally stored outside origin.
+
+Steps:
+1. Configure `checkpoint_remote` in `.entire/settings.json`.
+2. Push checkpoint refs to checkpoint remote.
+3. Ensure origin does not have v2 refs.
+4. Run command under test.

+git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/*'
+# Verify checkpoint remote has refs (replace <checkpoint-remote>)
+git ls-remote <checkpoint-remote> 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/*'
+```
+
+Expected:
+- Command reads/fetches from checkpoint remote successfully.
+
+### S5 v1 fallback
+
+Goal: validate legacy fallback while v1 support still exists.
+
+Steps:
+1. In a fresh branch/repo, create checkpoint with `checkpoints_v2=false`.
+2. Enable `checkpoints_v2=true` after that checkpoint exists.
+3. Confirm data exists on v1 branch and is absent from v2 refs.
+4. Run command under test.
+
+```bash
+# v1 should exist
+git show-ref --verify -- refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1 || true
+# v2 may be absent for this checkpoint
+git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main || true
+git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current || true
+```
+
+Expected:
+- Command succeeds via v1 fallback when checkpoint is not available in v2.
+
+### S6 Partial/missing artifacts
+
+Goal: validate error quality and fallback correctness under inconsistent storage states.
+
+Steps:
+1. Use a disposable clone only.
+2. Create one inconsistent state at a time:
+   - `/main` exists but missing `transcript.jsonl` for checkpoint.
+   - `/full/*` exists but missing `full.jsonl` for checkpoint.
+   - checkpoint subtree present in one ref but missing in another.
+3. Run command under test for each injected inconsistency.
+
+Expected:
+- Command either falls back correctly or fails with explicit, actionable error.
+- No silent success with wrong data source.
+
+### S7 Rotation + cleanup lifecycle
+
+Goal: validate archive creation and retention-based deletion.
+
+Steps:
+1. Generate enough checkpoints to create at least one archived generation.
+2. Confirm `generation.json` exists on archived refs.
+3. Configure retention to make a generation eligible (or use old timestamps in test data).
+4. Run `entire clean`.
+5. Compare local and remote archived refs before/after.
+
+Expected:
+- Only eligible archived generations are deleted.
+- `/main` and `/full/current` remain unchanged.

+
+Goal: validate v1-to-v2 migration and idempotency.

+Steps:

+2. Run `entire migrate` once.
+3. Verify split output (`/main` metadata/compact; `/full/current` raw).
+4. Run `entire migrate` again.
+5. Verify no duplicate logical checkpoint entries.
+
+Expected:
+- First run migrates all eligible checkpoints.
+- Second run is idempotent.

5: This is the command-first manual QA plan for the checkpoints v2 migration. It is intended to be used throughout rollout without needing rewrites as additional command support lands.
6: 
7: Goals:
8: - Validate v2 split-ref read/write behavior.
9: - Validate local-missing/remote-present fetch behavior.
10: - Validate rotation, cleanup, and migration lifecycle behavior.
11: - Provide copy-paste test steps and evidence collection.
12: 
13: ## v2 Invariants
14: 
15: - Permanent metadata + compact transcripts: `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main`
16: - Raw resumable logs: `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current`
17: - Archived raw generations: `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/<generation>`
18: - v1 fallback remains available until v1 removal
19: 
20: ## Global Test Setup
21: 
22: ### Test topology
23: 
24: Use three clones of one test repository:
25: - `repo-a`: primary writer and command runner
26: - `repo-b`: secondary writer for concurrency and remote edge cases
27: - `repo-fresh`: clean clone for fetch-on-demand tests
28: 
29: Optional: a dedicated checkpoint remote repository for `checkpoint_remote` scenarios.
30: 
31: ### Settings
32: 
33: Set strategy options in `.entire/settings.json`:
34: 
35: ```json
36: {
37:   "strategy_options": {
38:     "checkpoints_v2": true,
39:     "push_v2_refs": true,
40:     "generation_retention_days": 14
41:   }
42: }
43: ```
44: 
45: ### Baseline checks (run before each command section)
46: 
47: ```bash

49: git status --short --branch
50: # Confirm which branch the test is running on
51: git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD
52: # Verify v2 metadata ref exists locally (or not, for fallback scenarios)
53: git show-ref --verify -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main || echo "v2 main ref not found"
54: # Verify v2 raw current-generation ref exists locally
55: git show-ref --verify -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current || echo "v2 full/current ref not found"
56: # List all local v2 raw refs (current + archived generations)
57: git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/*'
58: # Verify legacy v1 branch presence for fallback tests
59: git show-ref --verify -- refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1 || echo "v1 checkpoints branch not found"
60: ```
61: 
62: ## Shared Inspection Toolkit
63: 
64: ### Ref checks
65: 
66: ```bash

68: git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main || echo "v2 main ref not found"
69: # Local v2 raw current ref hash (if present)
70: git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current || echo "v2 full/current ref not found"
71: # All local v2 raw refs with object IDs
72: git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short) %(objectname)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/*'
73: # Remote view of all v2 refs (origin)
74: git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/*'

76:

78: 
79: ```bash

125: ## Reusable Scenario Setup Guide
126: 
127: Use these scenario IDs in the command sections. Each scenario below includes concrete setup steps and expected state.

129: ### S1 Baseline v2 (checkpoint in `/main` and `/full/current`)

135: 2. Create a feature branch and produce one checkpoint via normal flow (`entire` hooks + one commit).
136: 3. Push branch and refs to origin.
137: 4. Verify checkpoint presence in both refs.

139: ```bash

141: git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main || echo "v2 main ref not found"
142: git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current || echo "v2 full/current ref not found"
143: # Verify v2 refs exist remotely
144: git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main'
145: git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current'
146: ```

148: Expected:
149: - `/main` and `/full/current` both exist and contain the new checkpoint shard.

151: ### S2 Archived generation (checkpoint only in `/full/<generation>`)
152: 
153: Goal: validate lookup behavior when raw transcript has rotated out of `/full/current`.

155: Steps:

168: - At least one `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/<number>` ref exists.

170: 
171: ### S3 Local missing / remote present
172: 
173: Goal: simulate a fresh/local-missing state and force fetch-on-demand behavior.
174: 
175: Recommended approach:
176: 1. Use `repo-fresh` clone (preferred, safest).
177: 2. Confirm refs exist on remote.
178: 3. Run command under test and verify refs/data are fetched as needed.

180: Disposable-clone approach (if not using `repo-fresh`):

190: done

192: git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/*'
193: ```
194: 
195: Expected:
196: - Local v2 refs are absent before test.
197: - Command succeeds when remote data exists and fetch path is implemented.
198: 
199: ### S4 `checkpoint_remote` only
200: 
201: Goal: verify behavior when checkpoint refs are intentionally stored outside origin.
202: 
203: Steps:
204: 1. Configure `checkpoint_remote` in `.entire/settings.json`.
205: 2. Push checkpoint refs to checkpoint remote.
206: 3. Ensure origin does not have v2 refs.
207: 4. Run command under test.
208: 
209: ```bash
210: # Origin should not have v2 refs in this scenario
211: git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/*'
212: # Verify checkpoint remote has refs (replace <checkpoint-remote>)
213: git ls-remote <checkpoint-remote> 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/*'
214: ```
215: 
216: Expected:
217: - Command reads/fetches from checkpoint remote successfully.
218: 
219: ### S5 v1 fallback
220: 
221: Goal: validate legacy fallback while v1 support still exists.
222: 
223: Steps:
224: 1. In a fresh branch/repo, create checkpoint with `checkpoints_v2=false`.
225: 2. Enable `checkpoints_v2=true` after that checkpoint exists.
226: 3. Confirm data exists on v1 branch and is absent from v2 refs.
227: 4. Run command under test.
228: 
229: ```bash
230: # v1 should exist
231: git show-ref --verify -- refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1 || echo "v1 checkpoints branch not found"
232: # v2 may be absent for this checkpoint
233: git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main || echo "v2 main ref not found"
234: git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current || echo "v2 full/current ref not found"
235: ```
236: 
237: Expected:
238: - Command succeeds via v1 fallback when checkpoint is not available in v2.

240: ### S6 Partial/missing artifacts
241: 
242: Goal: validate error quality and fallback correctness under inconsistent storage states.
243: 
244: Steps:
245: 1. Use a disposable clone only.
246: 2. Create one inconsistent state at a time:
247:    - `/main` exists but missing `transcript.jsonl` for checkpoint.
248:    - `/full/*` exists but missing `full.jsonl` for checkpoint.
249:    - checkpoint subtree present in one ref but missing in another.
250: 3. Run command under test for each injected inconsistency.
251: 
252: Expected:
253: - Command either falls back correctly or fails with explicit, actionable error.
254: - No silent success with wrong data source.
255: 
256: ### S7 Rotation + cleanup lifecycle
257: 
258: Goal: validate archive creation and retention-based deletion.
259: 
260: Steps:
261: 1. Generate enough checkpoints to create at least one archived generation.
262: 2. Confirm `generation.json` exists on archived refs.
263: 3. Configure retention to make a generation eligible (or use old timestamps in test data).
264: 4. Run `entire clean`.
265: 5. Compare local and remote archived refs before/after.
266: 
267: Expected:
268: - Only eligible archived generations are deleted.
269: - `/main` and `/full/current` remain unchanged.
270: 
271: ### S8 Migration lifecycle
272: 
273: Goal: validate v1-to-v2 migration and idempotency.
274: 
275: Steps:
276: 1. Prepare repository with v1-only checkpoint history.
277: 2. Run `entire migrate` once.
278: 3. Verify split output (`/main` metadata/compact; `/full/current` raw).
279: 4. Run `entire migrate` again.
280: 5. Verify no duplicate logical checkpoint entries.
281: 
282: Expected:
283: - First run migrates all eligible checkpoints.
284: - Second run is idempotent.
285: 
286: ## Command Matrix
287: 
288: | Command | What it does | Use it for | Required scenarios | Optional scenarios |
289: |---|---|---|---|---|
290: | `entire resume` | Restores agent session logs | Continue a prior coding session | S1 | S2, S3, S4, S5, S6 |
291: | `entire explain` | Reads and summarizes checkpoint context | Inspect what happened at a checkpoint | S1 | S3, S5, S6 |
292: | `entire doctor` | Checks checkpoint/ref health | Diagnose broken or missing checkpoint data | S1 | S3, S6, S7 |

<content>1: # Checkpoints v2 Manual Test Plan (Command-First)
2: 
3: ## Purpose
4: 
5: This is the command-first manual QA plan for the checkpoints v2 migration. It is intended to be used throughout rollout without needing rewrites as additional command support lands.
6: 
7: Goals:
8: - Validate v2 split-ref read/write behavior.
9: - Validate local-missing/remote-present fetch behavior.
10: - Validate rotation, cleanup, and migration lifecycle behavior.
11: - Provide copy-paste test steps and evidence collection.
12: 
13: ## v2 Invariants
14: 
15: - Permanent metadata + compact transcripts: `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main`
16: - Raw resumable logs: `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current`
17: - Archived raw generations: `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/<generation>`
18: - v1 fallback remains available until v1 removal
19: 
20: ## Global Test Setup
21: 
22: ### Test topology
23: 
24: Use three clones of one test repository:
25: - `repo-a`: primary writer and command runner
26: - `repo-b`: secondary writer for concurrency and remote edge cases
27: - `repo-fresh`: clean clone for fetch-on-demand tests
28: 
29: Optional: a dedicated checkpoint remote repository for `checkpoint_remote` scenarios.
30: 
31: ### Settings
32: 
33: Set strategy options in `.entire/settings.json`:
34: 
35: ```json
36: {
37:   "strategy_options": {
38:     "checkpoints_v2": true,
39:     "push_v2_refs": true,
40:     "generation_retention_days": 14
41:   }
42: }
43: ```
44: 
45: ### Baseline checks (run before each command section)
46: 
47: ```bash
48: # Verify v2 metadata ref exists locally (or not, for fallback scenarios)
49: git show-ref --verify -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main || echo "v2 main ref not found"
50: # Verify v2 raw current-generation ref exists locally
51: git show-ref --verify -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current || echo "v2 full/current ref not found"
52: # List all local v2 raw refs (current + archived generations)
53: git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/*'
54: # Verify legacy v1 branch presence for fallback tests
55: git show-ref --verify -- refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1 || echo "v1 checkpoints branch not found"
56: ```
57: 
58: ## Shared Inspection Toolkit
59: 
60: ### Ref checks
61: 
62: ```bash
63: # Local v2 metadata ref hash (if present)
64: git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main || echo "v2 main ref not found"
65: # Local v2 raw current ref hash (if present)
66: git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current || echo "v2 full/current ref not found"
67: # All local v2 raw refs with object IDs
68: git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short) %(objectname)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/*'
69: # Remote view of all v2 refs (origin)
70: git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/*'
71: ```
72: 
73: ### Checkpoint shard helper
74: 
75: Use the reusable executable script to determine the shard path.
76: 
77: ```bash
78: # Create helper script
79: cat > scripts/checkpoint-shard-path <<'EOF'
80: #!/usr/bin/env bash
81: set -euo pipefail
82: 
83: checkpoint_id="${1:-}"
84: if [ -z "$checkpoint_id" ]; then
85:   echo "usage: checkpoint-shard-path <checkpoint-id>" >&2
86:   exit 1
87: fi
88: 
89: echo "${checkpoint_id:0:2}/${checkpoint_id:2}"
90: EOF
91: 
92: # Make executable
93: chmod +x scripts/checkpoint-shard-path
94: 
95: # Usage
96: checkpoint_id="a3b2c4d5e6f7"
97: shard_path="$(scripts/checkpoint-shard-path "$checkpoint_id")"
98: echo "$shard_path"
99: ```
100: 
101: ### Tree/file checks
102: 
103: ```bash
104: # Show checkpoint directory in v2 permanent ref
105: git ls-tree --name-only refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main "$shard_path" || echo "checkpoint path not found on v2 main"
106: # Show checkpoint directory in v2 raw current generation
107: git ls-tree --name-only refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current "$shard_path" || echo "checkpoint path not found on v2 full/current"
108: # Read checkpoint summary metadata
109: git show "refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main:${shard_path}/metadata.json" || echo "metadata.json not found on v2 main"
110: # Read compact transcript (if compaction is available)
111: git show "refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main:${shard_path}/0/transcript.jsonl" || echo "transcript.jsonl not found on v2 main"
112: # Read raw transcript used by resume
113: git show "refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current:${shard_path}/0/full.jsonl" || echo "full.jsonl not found on v2 full/current"
114: # Read hash for raw transcript integrity
115: git show "refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current:${shard_path}/0/content_hash.txt" || echo "content_hash.txt not found on v2 full/current"
116: ```
117: 
118: ### Archived generation checks
119: 
120: ```bash
121: # List archived raw generations
122: git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/[0-9]*'
123: # Inspect generation retention timestamps
124: git show refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/0000000000001:generation.json || echo "generation.json not found for archived generation"
125: # Check whether checkpoint exists in a specific archived generation
126: git ls-tree --name-only refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/0000000000001 "$shard_path" || echo "checkpoint path not found in archived generation"
127: ```
128: 
129: ### v1 fallback checks
130: 
131: ```bash
132: # Verify legacy v1 metadata branch exists (for fallback)
133: git show-ref --verify -- refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1 || echo "v1 checkpoints branch not found"
134: # Check checkpoint path on v1 branch
135: git ls-tree --name-only entire/checkpoints/v1 "$shard_path" || echo "checkpoint path not found on v1"
136: # Read raw transcript from v1
137: git show "entire/checkpoints/v1:${shard_path}/0/full.jsonl" || echo "full.jsonl not found on v1"
138: ```
139: 
140: ## Custom Ref Primer (for this guide)
141: 
142: Use this section when a scenario asks you to add/remove or inspect v2 refs directly.
143: 
144: ```bash
145: # List local v2 refs
146: git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/*'
147: 
148: # Delete one local ref (safe in disposable clone)
149: git update-ref -d refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main
150: 
151: # Delete another local ref
152: git update-ref -d refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current
153: 
154: # Delete all local archived generation refs
155: for ref in $(git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/[0-9]*'); do
156:   git update-ref -d "$ref"
157: done
158: 
159: # Verify what still exists locally
160: git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/*'
161: 
162: # Verify what exists on origin (remote refs are unchanged by local delete)
163: git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/*'
164: ```
165: 
166: Notes:
167: - `git update-ref -d <ref>` deletes a **local ref pointer** only; it does not delete objects from remote.
168: - Destructive ref setup means intentionally deleting local checkpoint refs to simulate missing-data scenarios.
169: - Do this only in `repo-fresh` (or another disposable clone) so you do not lose local checkpoint state in your primary working clone.
170: - If you accidentally delete refs in the wrong clone, recover by fetching them again:
171: 
172: ```bash
173: git fetch origin refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main:refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main
174: git fetch origin refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current:refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current
175: ```
176: 
177: ## Command Test Plan
178: 
179: This guide is intentionally command-first. Each command section below includes self-contained setup, execution, checks, and expected outcomes.
180: 
181: ---
182: 
183: ## 1) `entire resume`
184: 
185: - What it does: restores the session transcript and prints the resume command.
186: - Use it for: continuing work from a checkpointed branch/session.
187: 
188: ### Scenario 1: Baseline v2 resume
189: 
190: Setup:
191: 1. In `repo-a`, enable `checkpoints_v2=true` and `push_v2_refs=true`.
192: 2. Create a feature branch and produce at least one checkpoint.
193: 3. Switch away from the feature branch.
194: 
195: Run:
196: 1. Execute `entire resume <feature-branch>`.
197: 
198: Checks:
199: 
200: ```bash
201: # Confirm local v2 metadata ref state before/after resume
202: git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main || echo "v2 main ref not found"
203: # Confirm local v2 raw current ref state before/after resume
204: git show-ref -- refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current || echo "v2 full/current ref not found"
205: # List all local raw refs to verify archived generation visibility
206: git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/*'
207: # Check remote metadata ref availability
208: git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main'
209: # Check remote raw refs availability
210: git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/*'
211: ```
212: 
213: Expected:
214: - Session restored and resume command printed.
215: - Checkpoint data resolves from v2 (`/full/current`).
216: 
217: ### Scenario 2: Resume from archived generation
218: 
219: Setup:
220: 1. In `repo-a`, generate enough checkpoints to rotate `/full/current`.
221: 2. Identify a checkpoint from before rotation.
222: 
223: Run:
224: 1. Execute `entire resume <branch-containing-older-checkpoint>`.
225: 
226: Expected:
227: - Resume succeeds using raw transcript from an archived `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/<generation>` ref.
228: 
229: ### Scenario 3: Local missing, remote present
230: 
231: Setup:
232: 1. Use `repo-fresh` clone (preferred), or delete local v2 refs in disposable clone.
233: 2. Confirm refs exist on remote.
234: 
235: ```bash
236: git update-ref -d refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main
237: git update-ref -d refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current
238: for ref in $(git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/[0-9]*'); do
239:   git update-ref -d "$ref"
240: done
241: git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/*'
242: ```
243: 
244: Run:
245: 1. Execute `entire resume <feature-branch>`.
246: 
247: Expected:
248: - Resume fetches required data and succeeds when remote data exists.
249: 
250: ### Scenario 4: `checkpoint_remote` source
251: 
252: Setup:
253: 1. Configure `checkpoint_remote`.
254: 2. Ensure v2 refs exist on checkpoint remote and not on origin.
255: 
256: Run:
257: 1. Execute `entire resume <feature-branch>`.
258: 
259: Expected:
260: - Resume succeeds by fetching metadata/transcripts from checkpoint remote.

# PR Feedback

## 1. Identify the PR

If the user provided a PR number or URL, use that. Otherwise, detect from the current branch:

Retrieve all pending review comments:

```bash

```bash
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/reviews --paginate

Filter to unresolved comments only. Ignore resolved threads and bot comments.

## 3. Parse and Group

For each comment, extract:
- **Author** — who left it
- **File and line** — where it points
- **Body** — the actual feedback
- **Thread context** — any replies in the same thread (to understand if it was already discussed)

Group comments that refer to the same issue or file region into a single finding.

## 4. Rank by Relevance

Present all findings in a numbered list, ordered by:

1. **Bugs / correctness issues** — reviewer identified broken logic or missing error handling
2. **Design / architecture feedback** — structural changes, API shape, naming of public interfaces
3. **Style / nits** — formatting, naming of local variables, minor readability

Work through the confirmed list one at a time:

1. State which finding you are addressing (number and one-line description)
2. Read the relevant code and the full comment thread to understand intent
3. Implement the fix — ONLY the changes needed for that single finding
4. Commit with a message referencing the feedback (e.g., `review: add nil check per @reviewer on ParseConfig`)
5. **STOP and wait for user approval** before proceeding to the next finding

NEVER batch multiple findings into one fix. NEVER proceed to the next finding without explicit user confirmation. The user may skip findings, reorder them, or stop the cycle at any point.

183: // classifySession determines if a session is stuck and returns diagnostic info.
184: // Returns nil if the session is healthy.
185: func classifySession(state *strategy.SessionState, repo *git.Repository, now time.Time) *stuckSession {
186: 	// Determine shadow branch info
187: 	shadowBranch := checkpoint.ShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
188: 	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranch)
189: 	_, refErr := repo.Reference(refName, true)
190: 	hasShadowBranch := refErr == nil
191: 
192: 	switch {
193: 	case state.Phase.IsActive():
194: 		// Active sessions are stuck if no interaction for over the staleness threshold
195: 		isStale := state.LastInteractionTime == nil || now.Sub(*state.LastInteractionTime) > stalenessThreshold
196: 		if !isStale {
197: 			return nil
198: 		}
199: 
200: 		var reason string
201: 		if state.LastInteractionTime != nil {
202: 			reason = fmt.Sprintf("active, last interaction %s ago", now.Sub(*state.LastInteractionTime).Truncate(time.Minute))
203: 		} else {
204: 			reason = "active, no recorded interaction time"
205: 		}
206: 
207: 		return &stuckSession{
208: 			State:             state,
209: 			Reason:            reason,
210: 			ShadowBranch:      shadowBranch,
211: 			HasShadowBranch:   hasShadowBranch,
212: 			CheckpointCount:   state.StepCount,
213: 			FilesTouchedCount: len(state.FilesTouched),
214: 		}
215: 
216: 	case state.Phase == session.PhaseEnded:
217: 		// Ended sessions are stuck if they have uncondensed data
218: 		if state.StepCount <= 0 || !hasShadowBranch {
219: 			return nil
220: 		}
221: 
222: 		return &stuckSession{
223: 			State:             state,
224: 			Reason:            "ended with uncondensed checkpoint data",
225: 			ShadowBranch:      shadowBranch,
226: 			HasShadowBranch:   hasShadowBranch,
227: 			CheckpointCount:   state.StepCount,
228: 			FilesTouchedCount: len(state.FilesTouched),
229: 		}
230: 
231: 	default:
232: 		return nil
233: 	}
234: }

237: func displayStuckSession(cmd *cobra.Command, ss stuckSession) {

241: 	fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Phase:   %s\n", ss.State.Phase)
242: 	fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Reason:  %s\n", ss.Reason)

255: 	}
256: 	fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Shadow branch: %s\n", shadowStatus)
257: 	fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Checkpoints: %d, Files touched: %d\n", ss.CheckpointCount, ss.FilesTouchedCount)
258: }

54: // shadowBranchPattern matches shadow branch names in both old and new formats:
55: //   - Old format: entire/<commit[:7+]>
56: //   - New format: entire/<commit[:7+]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>
57: //
58: // The pattern requires at least 7 hex characters for the commit, optionally followed
59: // by a dash and exactly 6 hex characters for the worktree hash.
60: var shadowBranchPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^entire/[0-9a-fA-F]{7,}(-[0-9a-fA-F]{6})?$`)
61: 
62: // IsShadowBranch returns true if the branch name matches the shadow branch pattern.
63: // Shadow branches have the format "entire/<commit-hash>-<worktree-hash>" where the
64: // commit hash is at least 7 hex characters and worktree hash is 6 hex characters.
65: // The "entire/checkpoints/v1" branch is NOT a shadow branch.
66: func IsShadowBranch(branchName string) bool {
67: 	// Explicitly exclude metadata and trails branches
68: 	if branchName == paths.MetadataBranchName || branchName == paths.TrailsBranchName {
69: 		return false
70: 	}
71: 	return shadowBranchPattern.MatchString(branchName)
72: }

74: // ListShadowBranches returns all shadow branches in the repository.
75: // Shadow branches match the pattern "entire/<commit-hash>" (7+ hex chars).
76: // The "entire/checkpoints/v1" branch is excluded as it stores permanent metadata.
77: // Returns an empty slice (not nil) if no shadow branches exist.
78: func ListShadowBranches(ctx context.Context) ([]string, error) {
79: 	repo, err := OpenRepository(ctx)
80: 	if err != nil {
81: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open git repository: %w", err)
82: 	}
83: 
84: 	refs, err := repo.References()
85: 	if err != nil {
86: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get references: %w", err)
87: 	}
88: 
89: 	var shadowBranches []string
90: 
91: 	err = refs.ForEach(func(ref *plumbing.Reference) error {
92: 		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
93: 			return err //nolint:wrapcheck // Propagating context cancellation
94: 		}
95: 		// Only look at branch references
96: 		if !ref.Name().IsBranch() {
97: 			return nil
98: 		}
99: 
100: 		// Extract branch name without refs/heads/ prefix
101: 		branchName := strings.TrimPrefix(ref.Name().String(), "refs/heads/")
102: 
103: 		if IsShadowBranch(branchName) {
104: 			shadowBranches = append(shadowBranches, branchName)
105: 		}
106: 		return nil
107: 	})
108: 	if err != nil {
109: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to iterate references: %w", err)
110: 	}
111: 
112: 	// Ensure we return empty slice, not nil
113: 	if shadowBranches == nil {
114: 		shadowBranches = []string{}
115: 	}
116: 
117: 	return shadowBranches, nil
118: }

120: // DeleteShadowBranches deletes the specified branches from the repository.
121: // Returns two slices: successfully deleted branches and branches that failed to delete.
122: // Individual branch deletion failures do not stop the operation - all branches are attempted.
123: func DeleteShadowBranches(ctx context.Context, branches []string) (deleted []string, failed []string, err error) { //nolint:unparam // already present in codebase
124: 	if len(branches) == 0 {
125: 		return []string{}, []string{}, nil
126: 	}
127: 
128: 	for _, branch := range branches {
129: 		// Use git CLI to delete branches because go-git v5's RemoveReference
130: 		// doesn't properly persist deletions with packed refs or worktrees
131: 		if err := DeleteBranchCLI(ctx, branch); err != nil {
132: 			failed = append(failed, branch)
133: 			continue
134: 		}
135: 
136: 		deleted = append(deleted, branch)
137: 	}
138: 
139: 	return deleted, failed, nil
140: }
